chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayyna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and more than one other, from them both (peace be upon them) together, that

they both said regarding the dog that the man sends (to hunt) while invoking God's name: 'If it (the dog) seizes it (the prey) and you reach it while it can still be slaughtered, then slaughter it; and if you reach it and it has already killed it and eaten from it, then eat what remains, and do not concern yourselves with what you are thinking regarding the dog.'

key_terms.الْكَلْب: The hunting dog — a trained dog used for lawful hunting; its use is permitted under specific conditions
key_terms.ذَكَاة: Ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah) — the act of properly slaughtering an animal according to Islamic law
key_terms.يُسَمِّي: Invokes God's name (Bismillah) — a condition for lawful slaughter and hunting

ai.seo_question: Is the prey caught by a hunting dog lawful to eat in Islam if the dog ate part of it?
ai.summary: This hadith records a joint ruling from Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both) on the permissibility of consuming prey caught by a hunting dog sent in the name of God. Two scenarios are addressed: if the prey is still alive when the hunter arrives, it must be ritually slaughtered; if the dog has already killed and partially eaten the prey, the remaining portion is lawful to consume. The closing phrase dismisses concerns about the dog's ritual impurity (najasah) contaminating the consumed meat — a common worry among early Muslim jurists.
